raw_response:
I have been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My husband passed years ago and my son works in the city now, so I manage most of it myself, though I pay a neighbor's son to run the machine for ploughing and harvesting. I have about 5 mu. I do not know how to do other crops — my neighbors all grow wheat and corn and so do I. That is what the soil here likes, that is what the buyers want, and that is what I know how to do.

For winter wheat, I will plant in October like always. I buy the improved seeds from the township supply store — the same kind I have used for several years now, the neighbors say it does well. I will put down compound fertilizer before ploughing and then add urea in spring when the green returns. I will water three times: once before winter sets in, once when the stem rises, once when the grain is filling. I do the spray twice — once for the weeds in winter, once in late spring for disease and insects all at once (一喷三防). My son hired a rotary tiller last autumn so the soil is still fine.

For summer corn, I plant right after the wheat machine harvests in June, no time to waste. I just scatter the seed into the stubble with no ploughing — that is how my neighbor does it and it saves my back. Hybrid seeds from the store. One watering if the rains are late. Spray twice — once for weeds early, once for the stem borer.

I will not try cotton or vegetables. Too much work at my age, and I do not know how to sell them.
